chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus al-Naysaburi al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, said: I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:

When the head of Al-Husayn was carried to Syria, Yazid - may God curse him - ordered it to be placed and a table spread over it. He and his companions began to eat and drink beer (fuqqa'). When they finished, he ordered the head to be placed in a tub under his couch, and a chessboard was spread over it. Yazid - may God curse him - sat playing chess, remembering Al-Husayn, his father, and his grandfather - may God's prayers be upon them - while mocking their memory. Whenever he defeated his companion, he took the beer and drank it three times, then poured the remainder onto the ground next to the tub.

So whoever is from our Shia should abstain from drinking beer and playing chess. And whoever looks at beer or chess should remember Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and curse Yazid and the family of Ziyad. God, the Mighty and Exalted, will erase his sins because of that, even if they were as numerous as the stars.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of abstaining from beer and chess in Shia tradition according to Al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (as) links the specific acts of drinking beer (*al-fuqaa'*) and playing chess (*al-shatranj*) to the historical mockery of Yazid and his court after the arrival of Al-Husayn’s head in Syria. This establishes a theological basis for these practices as acts of *istihza'* (mockery) against the Ahl al-Bayt, transforming them into opportunities for *dhikr* and *la'n* (cursing) that expiate sins, even those as numerous as the stars.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 30-50 Abdul Wahid Muhammad ibn Ubdoos al-Neishaboori al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba, on the authority of Al-Fadhl ibn Shathan that he had heard Al-Ridha (as) say, “

When they took the decapitated head of Al-Husayn (as) to Syria, Yazid - may God curse him - ordered that it be put somewhere and the tablecloth be spread. He and his companions started to eat and drink beer. When they finished eating, he ordered that they put the head in a tub in front of his couch and place the chess board over the tub. Yazid - may God curse him - started playing chess with his companions while he was swearing at Al-Husayn (as), his forefathers and grandfather (sw) and making fun of them. Whenever he won the game, he drank three mugs of beer. Then he poured down the little bit of leftover beer on the ground right next to the tub in which Al-Husayn’s (as) head was placed.

The Honorable the Exalted God will eliminate the sins of whoever sees beer or a chess board and remembers Al-Husayn (as), and curses Yazid and family of Ziyad, even if the number of his sins are as many as there are stars in the sky.”
